newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, EBRD to agree payment to shut Chernobyl.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, EBRD to agree payment to shut Chernobyl.

text.p: Ukraine and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) are close to signing an agreement to pay for the closure of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant, an EBRD official said on Monday.
"The agreement will be signed imminently so that work can proceed on the orderly closure of Chernobyl," Jaroslav Kinach, EBRD resident representative, told Reuters.

The plant was the site of the world's worst nuclear disaster in 1986, when its fourth reactor caught fire and exploded. It spewed fallout over most of Europe and contaminated large swathes of Ukraine.
The Ukrainian government has said 4,300 people died in the disaster.

Vyacheslav Mazurenko, senior official at Derzhkomatom, Ukraine's nuclear authority, told Interfax Ukraine news agency that Ukraine and the EBRD would hold joint tenders in January 1997 to find companies to shut the plant.
"To close it is a very complicated technical feat and a very expensive undertaking," Kinach said.

Kinach said it was difficult to determine exactly how much money the agreement was worth but said wealthy Group of Seven (G7) nations have agreed to fund up to $3 billion so that Ukraine can close the plant by the year 2000.

Kinach said the money would pay for Ukraine to replace electricity lost by Chernobyl's closure through construction of two new reactors at Khmelnitsky in southwest Ukraine and Rivne in western Ukraine, repair the concrete sarcophagus encasing the damaged fourth reactor and store nuclear fuel rods.
President Leonid Kuchma has pledged to close Chernobyl by 2000 to allay the fears of Western countries who say the plant is inherently unsafe.
But the government has complained that G7 countries are being too slow to release portions of the money promised to complete the shutdown.
Kinach said the funds will be provided through the EBRD's Nuclear Safety Account, which provides technical assistance to governments operating nuclear power plants considered unsafe.
He said the group targets Chernobyl-type RBMK reactors, the design of which is considered flawed.
